statements.text: For every such $X$, \begin{equation} \Q(X)\ge\mu\int_\Omega|X|^2, \end{equation} with equality exactly when $X=\grad v$ for some $v\in\V$.

statements.label: prop:multiplier
statements.text: For every real Lipschitz function $b$ on $\Sone$, \begin{equation} E(bg)=\frac12\iint N(s,t)(b(s)-b(t))^2 g(s)\cdot g(t)\dd s\dd t. \end{equation}

statements.label: thm:negative-kernel
statements.text: Let $\dd q=a\dd x$ on $\D$, where $a\in L^\infty(\D)$ is nonnegative, and suppose there is a constant $0<d<1$ such that \[ \int_\D|\psi|^2\dd q\le d\int_\D|\grad\psi|^2 \qquad(\psi\in H^1_0(\D)). \] For the associated kernels $K,N$ and every $p\in\D$, the kernel \begin{equation} D_p(s,t)=\frac{K(p,s)K(p,t)}{N(s,t)}\quad(s\ne t), \qquad D_p(s,s)=0, \end{equation} is conditionally negative semidefinite on $\Sone$.

statements.label: prop:interior-reciprocal

lean.scopeText: The strict hot-spots conjecture asks whether extrema of a first nonconstant Neumann eigenfunction occur only on the boundary. The formalization proves the stronger interior statement on every nonempty smooth bounded simply connected planar domain: every nonzero eigenfunction in the first positive Neumann eigenspace has nonvanishing gradient throughout the interior. Consequently all global maxima and minima lie on the boundary. The conclusion applies to every eigenfunction even when the eigenvalue is multiple.
